answer: Each identity claims one harbor yarrow stand, posts a 70-credit bond, and files a pollinator-visit table from its ledge transects, recording visits per hour per transect. Auditors recount a sample of transects; a count past tolerance burns the bond. The first fake costs 70 locked plus 400 fee, but stands are distinct, so the k-th fake needs a new stand, fee 400 plus 20 per earlier stand: the 1,000th fake pays 20,380 for it, and 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 and pay 10,390,000. Sharing a stand fails: each table matches one stand key. An honest agent claims one stand once, paying 70 plus 400.
